subject: Priority: service performance review, credit proposal, and exec sync request
messages:
From: Dana Gill <dana@hyperscale.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Cc: HyperScale Ops <ops@hyperscale.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Major latency & error spike — last 48 hours (SLO breach)

Marcus —

We saw sustained latency and a noticeable uptick in 5xx errors across our production RL-routing workload starting late Saturday and persisting through today. Our monitoring shows tail p95 latency degrading from ~230ms to ~1.1s and a sustained error rate bump from 0.05% to 1.8% during a 36-hour window. This triggered customer impact (user-facing timeouts) for several of our key flows.

I attached a short SLO extract and our service-side logs (slo_report_q3.pdf, redwood_service_log_export.csv). Please treat this as a priority: we need (1) a technical root-cause summary, (2) proposed remediation timeline, and (3) an initial calculation of contractual credits/remediation under our SLA. Our procurement & finance team will require documentation to process any credit.

We'd like an executive-level sync (our VP Product + our CFO cc'd) within 48 hours to align on next steps and confirm credit mechanics. Please propose times.

Thanks,
Dana Gill
Head of Platform
HyperScale Labs

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 12:15:45 -07:00
Subject: Internal: initial triage and proposed remediation (HyperScale)

Team — quick internal note from my triage:
- Signal summary: the error spike aligns with a degraded autoscaler decision path under sustained high short-lived bursts; we saw a cascade where incomplete KV cache warmups increased cold-start latency and pushed router timeouts.
- Root cause hypothesis: an edge case in the autoscaling controller where concurrent pod replacement + cache eviction led to a transient routing imbalance. This is reproducible in staging; patch available.

Proposed immediate remediation:
1) Roll a hotfix to autoscaler controller (non-disruptive patch) — ETA 6 hours to rollout and validate.
2) Backfill missing KV caches via background prewarm job — ETA 12 hours.
3) Temporary traffic shaping to route sensitive low-latency flows to regional pinned pools — immediate.

Commercial/credit recommendation (prelim):
- Based on the incident window and the contract SLA language (p95 & error rate thresholds), I estimate an initial service credit equivalent to 4–6% of the impacted billing period value. The attached worksheet (prelim_credit_calc.xlsx) has the raw math and sample invoice offsets. We should confirm with finance/legal.

I'll join the exec call if we need ops-level detail. Marcus — I need signoff to proceed with the hotfix and the traffic-shape change.

Eve
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Major latency & error spike — initial remediation plan & credit proposal

Dana / Matt —

Appreciate the patience while we triaged this. Brief summary and asks ahead of the exec sync:

What happened (short):
- We traced the spike to an autoscaler controller regression that, under a specific burst pattern, caused cache cold-starts and routing timeouts. Evelyn's team has a hotfix ready; we began staged rollout at 09:20 PT today.

Immediate remediation steps already underway:
- Hotfix rollout (in progress)
- Background KV prewarm job (started)
- We have pinned traffic for the highest-sensitivity routes to regional pools to limit exposure (temporary while we stabilize).

Preliminary credit proposal:
- Redwood proposes a 5% service credit on the invoice portion attributable to the impacted service for the month in which the incident occurred. We will provide a line-level workbook and a formal credit memo after we complete a full impact audit.

Executive sync:
- Proposed times (PT): Tue 1:30–2:00pm, Tue 3:00–3:30pm, Wed 09:00–09:30am. Please confirm preferred slot.

Docs attached: prelim_credit_calc.xlsx (workbook with assumptions), incident_summary_notes.txt (ops notes). Formal legal amendment language will be prepared if HyperScale prefers a one-off contract addendum rather than a stand-alone credit.

We want to make this right and will coordinate documentation your finance team needs.

—Marcus
VP, Customer Success Operations
Redwood Inference

Marcus / team —

Thanks for the quick remediation and the proposed 5% credit. We ran a second pass through our logs and procurement asked for a clearer mapping between impacted API routes and billed invoice lines before sign-off. Matt (CFO) would like to join the exec call on Tue 1:30pm PT; that slot works for us.

Two asks ahead of the call:
1) Please circulate the line-item workbook (invoice mapping) and the legal credit memo draft so our procurement can route approvals.
2) We'd prefer a cash credit applied to the next invoice rather than a service-use credit; please confirm whether Redwood can accommodate that. If cash is not possible under current commercial policy, propose the minimal amendment that would allow it.

We also want the contract amendment to include an SLA clause clarifying quantification methodology for multi-metric incidents (latency + error rate). I'll share a short suggested clause before the call.

Dana Gill
